thread:
andrea: starting a quick canary for runtime v2.3.1 — 5% traffic, 20m window. pinning console to 1.4.2 and keeping router on stable for now. change window 03:00-04:00 UTC. please watch latencies and 5xx rates.

deploy-bot: 🚀 Canary started: runtime v2.3.1 -> 5% traffic. Pins applied: console=1.4.2. Canary window ends at +20m. Track: /deploy/logs/6250000000

sam: thanks andrea. can we also pin API gateway to the same proto? last time mismatch caused header-swap 502s. @console-team fyi.

console-team: noted — console pinned to 1.4.2 by andrea. no DB migrations in this patch. :thumbsup:

kevin: quick heads-up — KV prefix cache coldstart observed in staging with v2.3.x. recommend issuing a small warmup traffic slice to avoid spikes. can do a curl-based warmup.

andrea: good call. planning a 1% warmup ramp for 5m before exposing 5% canary. updated deploy plan.

sre-oncall: seeing a small latency bump on a sample shard already (p50 +40ms) in early canary logs. nothing fatal yet but keeping eyes on p95. sending trace links.

kevin: paste warmup script here:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMUP_TOKEN" \"https://api.internal.runtime/health?key=prefix_$i\" >/dev/null
  sleep 0.2
done
```

rachel: /logs show some 502s clustered around router-az-b. small spike, ~0.3% of canary traffic, correlates with KV metrics. can we throttle that AZ while investigating?

router-team: we can steer traffic off az-b for the next 10m. proposing a traffic-slice update:

```yaml
traffic-split:
  az-a: 60
  az-b: 5  # drop from 35 to 5 for QA
  az-c: 35
```

andrea: implement that steer now. if 5xx exceeds 0.5% or p95 > 300ms we will abort and roll back to runtime v2.3.0. everyone ack?

sam: ack, monitoring metrics and traces. will notify if rollback criteria hit.

deploy-bot: traffic steer applied per request by andrea. New split: az-a=60, az-b=5, az-c=35.

sre-oncall: after steer p95 stabilized but there's a sustained error cluster in one router node. root cause unclear. logs show backend timeout 504 -> upstream write.

rachel: given the router node issue and KV coldstart, recommend pausing the canary, pin router to previous variant for affected shard, and run warmup + patch. less risky to pause than abort full rollout.

kevin: +1 to pause and warmup; patch is minor (reduce concurrent fetches during cache miss). can prepare a hotfix branch now.

andrea: i'm pausing the canary and scaling canary down to 0%. leaving console pinned. deploy-bot, execute pause.

deploy-bot: Canary paused by andrea. Runtime v2.3.1 traffic -> 0%. Console remains pinned at 1.4.2. Rolling back router routing changes? (yes/no)

rachel: please pin router back to v1.9.0 for the impacted shard while we validate hotfix.

router-team: pinned router shard-47 -> v1.9.0 (previous). routing rollback acknowledged.

andrea: plan: 1) pin router shard-47 (done), 2) hotfix runtime reducing concurrent KV fetches (kevin), 3) execute warmup on canary nodes for 10m, 4) re-run 5% canary with same checks. I'll include a release note line about the KV behavior.

sam: can you add a rollback clause in release notes: "Immediate pause + pin router on errors, rollback runtime to v2.3.0 if >0.5% 5xx"

andrea: added to release notes PR #444. change log updated. linking the PR: /github/redwood/runtime/pulls/444

deploy-bot: Note: scheduled follow-up job: run-warmup-6250000100 at +5m.

kevin: hotfix branch ready, running unit + staging smoke now. will tag for hotfix v2.3.1-hotfix1 if green.

rachel: thanks. will keep monitoring router logs and surface any anomalies. please ping #incidents if this expands. :eyes:

andrea: thanks team — good catch. keeping this thread for final rollforward decision. if kv warmup + hotfix look good, i will request a canary resume in ~30m.

sam: copy.

sre-oncall: monitoring dashboards: https://metrics.internal/redwood/dashboards/rollout-6250000000

deploy-bot: closing note: canary paused, tickets updated: #INC-7892, release note PR #444 linked."
